newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India premiums contract in light trade.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India premiums contract in light trade.

text.p: Some institutional selling of Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) on high premiums and strong U.S. payrolls data pushed prices slightly lower in London trade.
"Funds have taken the opportunity to sell some of the higher premium GDRs after recent gains, but it is nothing too heavy," said a London trader.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed down 0.38 points, 0.58 percent, at 71.28 points, with the premium over the local market at 21.61 percent compared with yesterday's 23.88 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index rose 55.93 points, or 1.66 pct to 3,418.32.
"The GDR market had been quite happy in thin trade before the U.S. figures, but was marked lower on stronger than expected payrolls," said one trader.
Amomg GDRs, hotels group EIH, which is on a premium of more than 51 percent over the local stock, fell 13 cents to 27.75.
"It is more a lack of buyers than any real selling pressure," said a trader.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended up 0.03 points at 64.48, a premium of 54.08 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index rose 12.92 points, or 2.02 percent, to 652.79.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended down 0.28 points at 96.63, a premium of 6.11 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index gained 84.01 points, 1.20 percent, to 7,094.77.
